_note: Machine-readable map of SOC 3300. verify_course.py --course 3300 checks the prose against this file. SOC 3300 is a 3000-level course on culture, media, and representation.

outcomes.LO1: Define culture sociologically and distinguish competing theories of it
outcomes.LO2: Analyse how cultural objects are produced, distributed, and consumed
outcomes.LO3: Apply encoding/decoding and representation theory to a media text
outcomes.LO4: Explain how cultural capital and taste mark social boundaries
outcomes.LO5: Read a media text as evidence of its historical moment
outcomes.LO6: Build and defend a cultural analysis of a single text

sessions.title: What Is Culture?
sessions.big_question: Is culture what a group has, or what a group does?

sessions.title: Ritual and Collective Effervescence
sessions.big_question: What does a group feel when it does something together — and why does it matter?

sessions.title: Cultural Production: Who Makes Culture
sessions.big_question: Who gets to make the culture the rest of us consume?

sessions.title: Encoding and Decoding
sessions.big_question: Why does a text mean different things to the people who made it and the people who watch it?

sessions.title: Representation and the Gaze
sessions.big_question: Who is looking at whom, and who gets to be the one looking?
sessions.episode_title: Sometimes You Get the Culture...Sometimes the Culture Gets You (second half)

sessions.title: The Sitcom as a Cultural Form
sessions.big_question: What can a sitcom say that other forms cannot?

sessions.title: The Black Sitcom and Its Audience
sessions.big_question: What does it mean for a genre to carry a community's image?

sessions.title: Language, Slang, and Identity
sessions.big_question: What does the way a community talks reveal about who it is and who belongs?

sessions.title: Music, Performance, and Identity
sessions.big_question: How does a step routine or a theme song carry identity?

sessions.title: Media Effects and Moral Panics
sessions.big_question: Does media change behavior, or does it change what we fear?

sessions.title: Audiences and Reception
sessions.big_question: What do audiences do with a text that its makers never intended?

sessions.title: Cultural Capital and Taste
sessions.big_question: How does what you like become who you are — and who you are not?

sessions.title: Memory, Nostalgia, and the Callback
sessions.big_question: What does it mean for a new show to keep calling back to an old one?

sessions.title: Culture as Resistance
sessions.big_question: When is a cultural act a political act?

sessions.title: Capstone: Reading a Text as Culture
sessions.big_question: Can you hold a whole text up to the course and read it as culture?
